meta.description: Not Woody Allen's joke. It was an anonymous quip, in print by 1938. Allen used a version in Annie Hall (1977), but the line was already old.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Sex is the most fun I ever had without laughing'?
meta.ogDescription: An anonymous quip, in print by 1938 and later pinned on Mencken, Bernhardt and Bogart. Woody Allen reused it in Annie Hall (1977). He didn't coin it.

answer.label: Not Woody Allen — an anonymous saying, in print by 1938
answer.sourceLine: Woody Allen did say a version of this, but he did not coin it. In Annie Hall (1977), his character Alvy Singer tells Annie after they first make love: “That was the most fun I’ve ever had without laughing.” Quote Investigator ↗ finds the joke already in print in Walter Winchell’s column of January 1938 as a “definition of necking,” which QI suspects was a cleaned-up version of a saying about sex. It concludes that an anonymous version about sex or love-making was in use by 1938. The popular wording, “Sex is the most fun I ever had…”, appears in no primary or documented source: it circulates on quote sites as a blend of the old “Sex is the most fun you can have without laughing” and Allen’s first-person screen line.

source.heading: The earliest documented version

docMeta.dd: Unidentified. Winchell gives it as “the latest definition,” not as his own.
Annie Hall (1977), spoken by Alvy Singer; screenplay by Woody Allen and Marshall Brickman

source.excerpt: The latest definition of necking: How you can have the most fun without laughing.
trail: 1938: Walter Winchell’s column gives “the latest definition of necking” with no author named. This is the earliest match found by Quote Investigator ↗ (also cited in Garson O’Toole’s ADS-L note ↗).
1942: H. L. Mencken’s A New Dictionary of Quotations prints “Love is the most fun you can have without laughing” and lists the author as “Author unidentified” (Quote Investigator ↗).

1967–1968: The “Sex is…” form appears. Leo Rosten jokes about a bestseller titled “Sex Is the Most Fun You Can Have Without Laughing,” and Evan Esar’s 20,000 Quips and Quotes prints the line unsigned (Quote Investigator ↗).
1977: In Annie Hall, Alvy Singer says after love-making: “That was the most fun I’ve ever had without laughing” (scene transcript at Filmsite ↗).
source.excerptNote: As transcribed by Quote Investigator. QI thinks Winchell, or whoever gave him the line, cleaned up an existing saying about sex to make it fit for a newspaper. Allen’s 1977 screen line is “That was the most fun I’ve ever had without laughing”. It does not begin “Sex is…”

source.rightsNote: No rights status can honestly be given for the popular wording. “Sex is the most fun I ever had without laughing” has no identifiable source. The earliest version, from 1938, is anonymous and after the 1931 U.S. public-domain cut-off. Allen’s own line is dialogue from Annie Hall (1977), a work still in copyright. quotle.info makes no public-domain claim for this line.

author.name: Woody Allen
author.heading: Woody Allen — he gave an old joke its most famous outing
author.metaLine: b. 1935 · American filmmaker, actor, writer and comedian
author.bio: Woody Allen is an American filmmaker, actor, writer and comedian. He holds the record for the most wins of the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay. Annie Hall (1977), which he directed and co-wrote with Marshall Brickman, won Best Picture and Best Original Screenplay. It is the source of the line people remember. He did not invent the joke. Quote Investigator finds it in print in 1938 with no author attached, and it was credited to several other famous names before Annie Hall.

misattribution.heading: Many famous names, no author
misattribution.intro: This joke has been credited to a long list of celebrities. Of the famous names below, Allen is the only one with a documented use of a version, and even he arrived after the joke had been in print for decades.

items.why: His character says “That was the most fun I’ve ever had without laughing” in Annie Hall (1977), a film he co-wrote with Marshall Brickman. Quote Investigator ↗ documents the saying from 1938 onward. The “Sex is… I ever had” wording is not the film line.
Mencken’s 1942 A New Dictionary of Quotations printed “Love is the most fun you can have without laughing” and credited it to “Author unidentified”. He did not claim it (Quote Investigator ↗).

In June 1942 the columnist E. V. Durling credited the “Love is…” version to the French actress, who had died in 1923. QI says it does not know whether she used a version in French (Quote Investigator ↗).

Bob Chieger’s 1983 collection Was It Good for You, Too? credited Bogart, who died in 1957, with “Nothing beats making love. It’s the most fun you can have without laughing.” QI finds earlier anonymous versions (Quote Investigator ↗).
Jim Bishop credited the radio comedian with a garbled version in columns of 1964 and 1972. Both postdate the 1938 printing (Quote Investigator ↗).

misattribution.truthLine: The joke is anonymous. Quote Investigator ↗ concludes that a version about sex or love-making was in use by 1938, and that Alfred Lunt, H. L. Mencken and E. V. Durling helped make it popular. Woody Allen’s Annie Hall gave it its best-known outing.

context.heading: Why the wrong name stuck
lead: The line people quote mixes two sources. The subject, “Sex is the most fun…”, comes from the anonymous saying, which by 1968 appeared in Evan Esar’s 20,000 Quips and Quotes as “Sex is the most fun you can have without laughing.” The first-person “I ever had” comes from Woody Allen’s scene in Annie Hall, where Alvy Singer says “That was the most fun I’ve ever had without laughing.” The blended version sounds like something Allen said, but no primary or documented source records it.

The joke had a long life before Allen. Quote Investigator ↗ notes that its first known printing, in 1938, was about “necking”. QI’s explanation is that the taboos of the time kept frank talk of sex out of newspapers. Over the following decades the line was credited to Sarah Bernhardt, to a radio comedian, and, after the film, to Humphrey Bogart.
context.pull: That was the most fun I’ve ever had without laughing. — Alvy Singer, Annie Hall (1977)

sourcesVerified.claim: Earliest match QI found is Winchell's column of 25 January 1938 (Wilkes-Barre Times Leader, p. 24): 'The latest definition of necking: How you can have the most fun without laughing.' QI concludes an anonymous version about sex or love-making was in use by 1938.

Mencken's 1942 dictionary prints 'Love is the most fun you can have without laughing' with 'Author unidentified'; Durling credited it to Sarah Bernhardt in June 1942 (she died in 1923); Rosten used it in 1967; Esar printed the 'Sex is...' form in 1968; Bishop credited Colonel Stoopnagle in 1964 and 1972; Chieger credited Bogart in 1983 (he died in 1957).
In Annie Hall (1977), co-written by Allen and Marshall Brickman, Alvy Singer says after making love: 'That was the most fun I've ever had without laughing.'
Filmsite's scene account transcribes Alvy's line after the first love scene: 'That was the most fun I've ever had without laughing.'
O'Toole's ADS-L post cites the 1938 Winchell column and Mencken's 1942 'Author unidentified' entry, and names earlier research by Nigel Rees, Fred Shapiro and Ralph Keyes.
Annie Hall is a 1977 film directed by Woody Allen from a screenplay by Allen and Marshall Brickman. It won Best Picture, and Allen and Brickman won Best Original Screenplay.
Woody Allen is an American filmmaker, actor, writer and comedian, born in 1935, who holds the record for most Best Original Screenplay wins (3).
